summary: HETA combines causal attention–value flow, Hessian–vector sensitivity, and KL masking into a decoder-only token attribution method, with multi-model experiments, ablations, and a curated distractor dataset that appear competitive against recent generative baselines. The core idea is useful but largely an incremental fusion of known components, and the paper’s central new metric (DSA) is mathematically inconsistent with the reported scores under the stated normalization. Overclaims (e.g., “human” alignment via GPT annotators; “new standard”) plus ambiguous score composition weaken soundness enough that this is below the clear ICLR accept bar without substantial clarification and re-validation.
strengths: Targets a real gap: faithful, target-conditioned attribution for decoder-only generation rather than encoder-style feature attribution.

Broad empirical sweep: multiple decoder-only scales (GPT-J, Phi-3, LLaMA-70B, Qwen), strong recent baselines (ContextCite, ReAgent, TDD, SEA-CoT, etc.), component ablations, and robustness to noise, paraphrase, and decoding hyperparameters.
Method description includes practical scalability choices (HVP/Hutchinson, optional low-rank/windowing/layer sampling) with reported compute settings that support reproducibility of the procedure.
Curated NarrativeQA+SciQ distractor construction is a clear, interpretable probe for whether attributions prefer diagnostic vs. irrelevant context.

key_concerns.issue: DSA is defined with per-paragraph attributions normalized to sum to one (implying DSA = mass_SciQ − mass_NarrQA ∈ [−1, 1]), yet Table 1 reports HETA scores of 4.25–5.10 (and other methods >2). This contradiction undermines the main alignment claim and the curated-benchmark contribution.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Publish a single unambiguous DSA formula, prove the admissible range, regenerate Table 1 under that definition, and release instance-level score checks; if scores are ratios/logits/unnormalized, revise the text and all claims accordingly.

key_concerns.issue: The abstract claims alignment with human annotations, but gold labels are intersections of GPT-4o and GPT-5 annotations. That is LLM-as-judge, not human evaluation, and risks circularity when evaluating LLM attributions.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Replace “human” wording with accurate LLM-annotator language, add a human-labeled subset with agreement vs. GPT labels, and report sensitivity of rankings to the annotator choice.

key_concerns.issue: Final score Attr = M_T[i] β S_i + γ I(·) is notationally ambiguous (gate over both terms vs. only the Hessian term) and the β,γ fusion is largely heuristic; Soft-NC gains of ~2× over the next best method are extreme and not tightly tied to a verified causal claim.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Write an unambiguous equation, justify or learn β/γ with a held-out protocol, add controls that isolate each term’s contribution to Soft-NC/DSA, and report significance tests / confidence intervals beyond mean±std over 3 runs.

key_concerns.issue: Novelty is primarily combining attention-rollout/value norms, Hessian/HVP sensitivity, and occlusion-style KL—each well known—without a sharp uniqueness result beyond the product/gate recipe.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Sharpen contribution claims vs. Kobayashi-style value-weighted attention, Hessian attribution, and ReAgent/ContextCite; add head-to-head ablations against strong single-component upgrades of those priors.

key_concerns.issue: Limitations text is partly generic boilerplate, while the stronger runtime/memory/long-context trade-offs are under-emphasized relative to “new standard” rhetoric.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Lead with concrete cost–quality trade-offs (full vs. LR+WIN vs. last-six-layers) and scope claims to evaluated models/tasks.

questions_for_authors: Under the stated unit-mass normalization, how can DSA exceed 1.0 in Table 1, and what exact aggregation is averaged across instances?
Is M_T[i] multiplicative over (β S_i + γ I_i), only over S_i, or something else—and how were β=γ=0.5 selected without overfitting to the curated set?
What fraction of Soft-NC/DSA gains remains if Hessian terms use a Gauss–Newton/Fisher surrogate only, or if KL masking uses a fixed neutral token vs. deletion?
Do Soft-NC/Soft-NS and DSA rankings change on a human-annotated subset, and what is agreement between GPT annotators and humans on support spans?
For LLaMA-3.1-70B, how much do results move when second-order terms are computed on all layers vs. the last six only?
calibration_check: Claims of consistently superior faithfulness and especially “human” alignment / a “new standard” are ahead of the evidence given the DSA definition–table mismatch, LLM-only labels, and heuristic score fusion.

significance.justification: Faithful decoder-only attribution matters to the XAI/LLM community, but impact hinges on fixing metric validity and would likely be cited as a useful recipe rather than a foundational advance.

novelty.justification: Core contribution is a weighted combination of known causal rollout/value flow, Hessian–vector sensitivity, and KL masking rather than a distinctly new attribution principle.

rigor.justification: Method motivation is reasonable, but ambiguous Attr composition and especially DSA’s inconsistency with reported magnitudes break the claim–evidence link for the headline alignment results.

statistical_soundness.justification: Means over three runs with small reported stds and multi-seed decoding grids help, yet formal significance tests are absent and unexplained ~2× Soft-NC margins invite skepticism.

calibration_honesty.justification: “Human annotations,” “new standard,” and large DSA numbers are not adequately scoped to LLM labels, heuristic fusion, and the stated normalization constraints.

clarity.justification: Overall narrative is followable and structured, but critical equations (Attr, DSA) and some table text are ambiguous or internally conflicting.

structure_compliance.justification: Contains abstract, intro, motivation/background, method, experiments, related work, conclusion/limitations in a recognizable conference organization of reasonable length.

reproducibility.justification: Models, β/γ, sequence lengths, HVP/low-rank/windowing/layer-sampling choices, and evaluation metrics are described sufficiently to reimplement absent redacted links.

related_work.justification: Positions against attention, IG, ContextCite, TDD, Peering, and ReAgent with mostly fair contrasts, though uniqueness vs. value-weighted attention and Hessian XAI priors could be sharper.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe an informative pipeline figure, component ablations, robustness panels, and qualitative importance maps that directly support the stated claims.

breadth_generality.justification: Four decoder-only models, three public generative benchmarks plus a curated set, many baselines, and robustness/ablation suites adequately support the scoped decoder-only claims.

overall_recommendation.justification: Promising empirical package for ICLR, but blocking metric inconsistency and major honesty/novelty gaps place it at borderline reject pending substantial revision.
